Definition: from G1332; a space of two years (biennium):--two years.
BiblicalUsage: Two years is the time Paul spends in his own hired house in Rome, and the word stands twice for it. He is kept two years under Felix, and he dwells two whole years in Rome receiving all who come to him and preaching the kingdom with all confidence.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two years in Rome are the quiet triumph of the gospel; Paul is a prisoner, and yet the word is not bound, and the hired house becomes a church where the kingdom is preached without hindrance.
